glosses: In or to all locations under discussion.

examples.text: He delivers the mail everywhere on this street.

Risk is everywhere. From tabloid headlines insisting that coffee causes cancer (yesterday, of course, it cured it) to stern government warnings about alcohol and driving, the world is teeming with goblins. For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you.

glosses: In or to a few or more locations.

examples.text: We went to Europe last year and went everywhere: Berlin, Paris, London, and Madrid.
When I shop for shoes, I like to look everywhere.
I've looked everywhere in the house and still can't find my glasses.
I went out to get some groceries, but everywhere was closed.

glosses: Over a great distance or large area; nearly everywhere.
Implying a lengthy, exhausting or unpleasant experience.

examples.text: I just spent two hours in the dentist's chair. Thank God it's all over.
Just as soon as Christmas arrives, it seems it's all over.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: all over.

examples.text: It's the final fence ... and ... the horses are all over!

I've looked all over for it.
I'm itching all over.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: all over.

examples.text: He dropped the bucket and got paint all over the floor and his clothes.

glosses: In every part of; all through.

examples.text: And though a philosopher may live remote from business, the genius of philosophy, if carefully cultivated by several, must gradually diffuse itself throughout the whole society.

examples.text: Thus the VON VÖLCKER of Frankfurt bear : Argent, a rose gules, the field embrassé à senestre of the second. We should blazon this : Gules, a pile throughout issuing from the dexter flank, charged with a rose of the field.

glosses: En tous lieux ; en tous endroits ; de tous côtés.
